state_sync.note: The original 25-unit local gap was already closed by the Algorithmist after the mission message. External inequalities below are therefore sought for independent explanation, strengthening, generalization, or barrier evidence.

exact_problem_fingerprint.operation: compatible coordinatewise signed union; a POS/NEG clash makes a pair tautological and excluded
exact_problem_fingerprint.objective: upper-bound the number J and/or total support mass of distinct new outputs under omission/incidence constraints
exact_problem_fingerprint.dangerous_historical_regime: J>=610 would force at least 610 of 616 parent pairs to have distinct new compatible outputs, i.e. a near-injective partial join map

top_10.source: Holzman-Korner entropy inequality as quoted and developed by Janzer
top_10.primary: R. Holzman, J. Korner, Cancellative pairs of families of sets, European Journal of Combinatorics 16 (1995) 263-266
top_10.theorem_statement: For a cancellative pair (A,B), if p_i is the fraction of A omitting coordinate i and q_i the fraction of B omitting i, then log2(|A||B|) <= sum_i [p_i h(q_i)+q_i h(p_i)]. The same line yields |A||B| < 2.3264^n.
top_10.exact_model_assumptions: Two families of subsets of one n-element Boolean ground set; for fixed B the union map A->A union B is injective, and symmetrically for fixed A.
top_10.resource_required: Coordinate omission marginals plus exact cancellativity.
top_10.candidate_janus_insertion_point: N58 signed-parent omission marginals a_y/|P| and b_y/|Q|; possible entropy analogue of the internal incidence-support inequality.
top_10.applicability: HIGH structural match: both arguments are coordinatewise and driven by omission marginals.
top_10.non_applicability: JANUS has signed ternary coordinates, partial compatibility, retained clauses, and only a near-injective dangerous regime; ordinary cancellativity is not established.

top_10.primary: Barnabas Janzer, A New Upper Bound for Cancellative Pairs, Electronic Journal of Combinatorics 25(2) P2.13 (2018)
top_10.theorem_statement: Every cancellative pair on an n-element Boolean ground set satisfies |A||B| <= 2.2682^n.
top_10.exact_model_assumptions: Ordinary subset families and exact cancellativity; proof refines coordinate-entropy bounds and uniform reductions.
top_10.resource_required: Exact cancellativity and Boolean-coordinate entropy structure.
top_10.candidate_janus_insertion_point: Search for a signed/partial-join analogue with the N58 omission vector constrained by regular incidence.
top_10.applicability: Strong method analogue; paper exposes the coordinate optimization explicitly.
top_10.non_applicability: The constant 2.2682 cannot be applied to six signed coordinates by treating each sign as an ordinary Boolean coordinate without losing the JANUS constraints.

top_10.primary: Zoltan Furedi, Hypergraphs in which all disjoint pairs have distinct unions, Combinatorica 4 (1984) 161-168
top_10.theorem_statement: For an r-uniform family L on an n-set, r>=3, if |L| > 3.5*C(n,r-1), then four distinct members A,B,C,D exist with A union B = C union D and A intersect B = C intersect D = empty.
top_10.exact_model_assumptions: One unsigned r-uniform family; collision is between two disjoint pairs from that family.
top_10.candidate_janus_insertion_point: Collision-forcing control for the near-injective resolvent-output map.
top_10.applicability: Directly studies how many pair-unions can stay distinct before collisions become forced.
top_10.non_applicability: JANUS is bipartite, signed, nonuniform, partially compatible and has retained-output exclusions.

top_10.primary: Peter Frankl, An Extremal Problem for two Families of Sets, European Journal of Combinatorics 3 (1982) 125-127
top_10.theorem_statement: If |A_i|=r, |B_i|=s, A_i intersect B_i=empty, and A_i intersect B_j != empty for i<j, then m <= C(r+s,s).
top_10.exact_model_assumptions: Indexed paired families, fixed cardinalities r,s, diagonal disjointness and directional cross-intersection.
top_10.resource_required: A valid encoding of output representatives as indexed set-pairs satisfying the cross-intersection premise.
top_10.candidate_janus_insertion_point: Potential representative-pair ceiling if tautology/compatibility conditions can be converted into the required skew cross-intersection matrix.
top_10.applicability: Bipartite two-family theorem with an exact finite binomial ceiling.
top_10.non_applicability: The required indexed cross-intersection condition has not been proved for JANUS parent/resolvent representatives.

top_10.primary: Peter Frankl, Zoltan Furedi, Union-free families of sets and equations over fields, Journal of Number Theory 23 (1986) 210-218
top_10.theorem_statement: For a k-uniform family F in which all unordered pair-unions are distinct, |F| has matching polynomial-order upper/lower bounds c_k n^{ceil(4k/3)/2} and c'_k n^{ceil(4k/3)/2} for fixed k.
top_10.exact_model_assumptions: Single unsigned k-uniform family; every pair-union distinct.
top_10.applicability: The exact phenomenon is uniqueness of pair unions.
top_10.non_applicability: Asymptotic unsigned one-family theorem; N58 is six-coordinate bipartite signed partial union.

top_10.primary: Rudolf Ahlswede, Gabor Simonyi, On the optimal structure of recovering set pairs in lattices: the sandglass conjecture, Discrete Mathematics 128 (1994) 389-394
top_10.theorem_statement: Defines recovering pairs by injective join/meet recovery in a lattice; for a product of two finite chains the maximum product size is achieved by a sandglass.
top_10.exact_model_assumptions: A genuine lattice that is a product of two finite chains; both join- and meet-recoverability conditions.
top_10.resource_required: Total lattice join/meet and recovery premises.
top_10.candidate_janus_insertion_point: Investigate the six-coordinate signed-tail space as a partial join structure and search for an appropriate lattice completion that preserves counting authority.
top_10.applicability: Moves cancellative/recovering combinatorics from Boolean sets to lattices/product structures.
top_10.non_applicability: The JANUS coordinate poset {OMIT,POS,NEG} has incompatible POS/NEG with no join inside the three-state space and is not a chain product.

top_10.primary: L. D. Meshalkin, Generalization of Sperner's Theorem on the Number of Subsets of a Finite Set, Theory of Probability and Its Applications 8 (1963) 203-204
top_10.theorem_statement: For decompositions of an n-set into r disjoint parts under the stated coordinatewise non-comparability condition, the maximum family size equals the largest multinomial coefficient n!/(n_1!...n_r!).
top_10.exact_model_assumptions: Complete r-part decompositions and Meshalkin's non-connected/non-comparability condition between every pair of decompositions.
top_10.resource_required: A proof that the relevant JANUS signed vectors form such a decomposition antichain.
top_10.candidate_janus_insertion_point: Encode each tail as the 3-part decomposition POS / NEG / OMIT and test whether canonical-CNF/incidence constraints imply a Meshalkin-type antichain.
top_10.applicability: The three-way coordinate decomposition matches the signed-tail representation exactly at the encoding level.
top_10.non_applicability: The required antichain condition is not currently established, so the multinomial ceiling cannot yet be imported.

top_10.primary: Joseph B. Kruskal, The Number of Simplices in a Complex, Mathematical Optimization Techniques (1963) 251-278
top_10.theorem_statement: The size of the lower shadow of a uniform set family is minimized by the corresponding initial colex segment; equivalently the binomial representation of family size gives an exact lower-shadow bound.
top_10.exact_model_assumptions: Unsigned k-uniform subsets of an n-element ground set and the standard subset shadow operator.
top_10.resource_required: A faithful mapping from resolvent support layers to a Boolean/uniform shadow problem.
top_10.candidate_janus_insertion_point: Potential strengthening of Wmax/support-mass occupancy by constraining how many low-support outputs can coexist with their required shadows.
top_10.applicability: Exact finite layer/shadow inequality, potentially relevant to support mass.
top_10.non_applicability: JANUS outputs are signed and nonuniform; no shadow-closure property has been proved.

top_10.primary: Gyula O. H. Katona, Shadows of finite sets, Journal of Combinatorial Theory 4 (1968) 40-48
top_10.theorem_statement: Proves a union-shadow bound theorem controlling the shadow of a union of set families from bounds on the individual shadows, together with a recursive inequality.
top_10.exact_model_assumptions: Ordinary finite set families and the inclusion-graph shadow operator; cardinality layers are specified in the theorem.
top_10.resource_required: A justified shadow representation for the distinct resolvent output family.
top_10.candidate_janus_insertion_point: Support occupancy / layer interaction rather than raw pair count.
top_10.applicability: May couple output counts across support sizes, precisely where Wmax is currently intentionally loose.
top_10.non_applicability: No signed-shadow theorem or required closure property has yet been derived for the N58 output family.

top_10.primary: Bela Bollobas, Imre Leader, An Erdos-Ko-Rado Theorem For Signed Sets, Computers and Mathematics with Applications 34(11) (1997) 9-13
top_10.theorem_statement: An intersecting family of signed r-sets on [n] has size at most 2^(r-1)*C(n-1,r-1).
top_10.exact_model_assumptions: Every member has exactly r active coordinates; any two signed sets share an active coordinate carrying the same sign.
top_10.resource_required: A proof that a relevant parent/output subfamily satisfies signed intersection rather than mere compatibility.
top_10.candidate_janus_insertion_point: Signed-set finite ceiling control and possible subfamily decomposition by support size.
top_10.applicability: Works directly with +/- signs rather than encoding them as independent Boolean elements.
top_10.non_applicability: JANUS requires cross-family non-conflict/distinct-union counting, not same-family signed intersection.

priority_red_summary: INTERNAL_RED: the historical 25-unit gap is already closed by Algorithmist at raw<=3361, so do not report 3389 as current.
EXTERNAL_RED_CANDIDATE: Holzman-Korner/Janzer coordinate-entropy machinery uses the same type of omission marginals as the N58 incidence proof, but a signed partial-join generalization is required.
MODEL_RED_CANDIDATE: recovering-pair lattice theory is conceptually close, but the ternary signed coordinate object is not a product of chains and has undefined joins for opposite signs.
NO_DIRECT_EXTERNAL_INEQUALITY_FOUND_YET that matches all N58 assumptions and independently yields a new exact raw-unit ceiling.
